h1: The 6 Best Electric Food Choppers Under $75, Corded and Cordless, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Electric Food Chopper Under $75: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 electric food choppers around the $75 mark, corded and cordless, scored on capacity, motor, cleanup and kitchen footprint.
summary: The KitchenAid 5 Cup Food Chopper is the best electric chopper for a household in this range, with a bowl big enough for sauces and dips. The Ninja Express Chop 200W is the best small chopper, the Hamilton Beach cordless mini is the one to carry anywhere, and the BLACK+DECKER is the cheapest to own and clean.
intro: Seventy-five dollars is an awkward budget for a chopper. It is more than the cheapest minis cost, and less than a true food processor, so you land in a band where bowl size and brand are the real choices. The temptation is to pay for the brand name; the better question is how much you chop at once, because a bowl that is too small ruins the point of owning one.

Six choppers are ranked below, from a 1.5-cup budget unit to a 5-cup KitchenAid. Two KitchenAid listings and the cordless Hamilton Beach did not confirm an exact price tier in our data, so verify the current price. Scoring covers capacity, motor, control, cleaning and portability.

products.name: KitchenAid 5 Cup Food Chopper KFC0516ER
products.verdict: A 5-cup chopper in Empire red with room for a family-size batch of salsa or pesto.
products.description:
The KFC0516ER is a 5-cup KitchenAid chopper in an Empire red finish. It is the largest bowl in this ranking.

Five cups means a full batch of salsa, hummus or chimichurri in one go, where a 16-ounce mini would need three rounds. That is why it leads for households. The listing gives no motor wattage or blade information, and our data did not confirm a price tier, so check the current price against your $75 limit.

Buy it if you cook sauces for a family. Skip it if you only mince garlic.
pros: Five cup bowl is the largest here

products.name: Ninja Food Chopper Express Chop 200W
products.verdict: 200W and 16 ounces, built for mincing, grinding and blending in small amounts.
products.description:
The Ninja Express Chop has a 200W motor and a 16-ounce bowl and handles mincing, chopping, grinding and blending. It sits in the $25 to $50 bracket.

It takes second place because it is the best small chopper, with a motor that stays calm on spices and nuts. Compared with the KitchenAid, it gives up volume but costs far less and stores in a drawer. Grinding coffee beans or spices is a role the larger choppers rarely advertise.

Buy it if you chop and grind small quantities. Skip it if you need a big bowl.

products.name: Hamilton Beach Powerful Cordless Mini Food Processor
products.verdict: A rechargeable mini vegetable chopper that works without an outlet.
products.description:
This Hamilton Beach is a cordless mini food processor aimed at vegetable chopping. Our data lists it in the $50 to $100 bracket, so check that the current price sits under $75.

The cordless design means you can chop at a picnic table, a campsite or the far side of a kitchen with no cord to snag. The trade is run time per charge and power, and the listing gives neither capacity nor battery life. It ranks third because it asks you to pay for portability that many kitchens do not need.

Buy it if outlets are scarce. Skip it if you chop heavily.

products.name: Cuisinart Mini Food Processor
products.verdict: A 3-cup mini with a reversible blade and the Cuisinart name.
products.description:
The Cuisinart Mini has a 3-cup capacity and a reversible blade, in the $25 to $50 bracket.

The blade flips between a sharp edge for cutting and a dull one for grinding or mixing, giving one blade two personalities. Three cups sits between the Ninja and the KitchenAid. It ranks fourth because it is solid but undramatic, and the listing does not give motor power.

Buy it if you want a middle-size bowl from a trusted brand. Skip it if you want listed wattage.
products.idealFor: Sauces and spreads in modest batches.

products.name: KitchenAid 3.5 Cup Food Chopper KFC3516CU
products.verdict: A 3.5-cup chopper in Contour silver for couples and small kitchens.
products.description:
The KFC3516CU holds 3.5 cups and comes in Contour silver. Our data did not confirm its price tier.

It makes sense if you want KitchenAid styling and a modest bowl, since it covers most daily needs for one or two people. It ranks fifth because the 5-cup sibling gives more room for a similar outlay and the listing gives no wattage.

Buy it if you want the silver finish and a small footprint. Skip it if you prefer the bigger bowl.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 1.5-Cup Electric Food Chopper
products.verdict: A 150W, 1.5-cup chopper with pulse control and dishwasher-safe parts for under $25.
products.description:
The BLACK+DECKER has a 150W motor, a 1.5-cup bowl, a one-touch pulse button, a stay-sharp blade and dishwasher-safe parts, all in the under $25 bracket.

It ranks last in this field only for size. For garlic, shallots and herbs, the pulse button and easy cleanup do the work, and you save most of your budget. Spending more only makes sense if you need a bigger bowl.

Buy it if you chop small amounts and want to spend little. Skip it if you make sauces for a family.
products.idealFor: Small jobs on a small budget.

whatMatters.detail: A corded motor delivers steady power for as long as you need. A cordless chopper trades that for portability and a limited run time. For frequent chopping, corded is the safer choice.
A 1.5 cup bowl suits garlic and herbs, while 5 cups handles a family dip. If you often repeat runs, the bowl is too small. Pick one that fits your usual batch.
Pulse buttons give you texture control. Without one you chop for a set time and get paste. Look for a pulse function on the listing.
KitchenAid, Cuisinart and Hamilton Beach parts are easy to find if a bowl cracks. Unknown brands can leave you without a replacement.
Dishwasher-safe parts and wide bowls save time. Blades are sharp, so lift them by the hub. A chopper that is a chore to clean ends up in the cupboard.

faq.q: Is a chopper the same as a food processor?
faq.a: No. A chopper has one blade and chops. A processor has discs for slicing and shredding as well. Choose based on your recipes.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying one?
faq.a: Buying too small a bowl. Repeat runs defeat the point. Match the bowl to your usual batch.

faq.q: Is the KitchenAid worth it over the Ninja?
faq.a: For batch cooking, yes. For small tasks and grinding, the Ninja is cheaper and compact.

faq.q: How long does a cordless chopper run?
faq.a: The listing does not say. Expect short bursts, and charge it after use.

faq.q: How do I clean the blade safely?
faq.a: Hold it by the plastic hub, wash with a brush under running water and dry carefully. Never wipe the edge with your fingers.
Yes, in short pulses. Overprocessing turns nuts into butter.

finalTake: The KitchenAid 5 Cup Food Chopper is the best electric chopper around $75, with the biggest bowl and the sturdiest brand behind it. The Ninja Express Chop 200W is the best small and spice-friendly option, and the BLACK+DECKER is the cheapest to run. Check the current price of the KitchenAid and the cordless Hamilton Beach before you buy.
